title: OpenAI countersues Apple, accusing it of taking trade secrets and pressuring suppliers
dek: The counterclaims answer Apple's July lawsuit over OpenAI's hardware plans. Apple calls them 'a transparent attempt to distract'.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
OpenAI has filed counterclaims against Apple in a federal court in California, accusing the iPhone maker of obtaining its trade secrets through a rehired employee and of pressuring shared hardware suppliers not to work on OpenAI's planned AI devices. The filing on Friday, in the federal court in San Jose, answers a lawsuit Apple brought against OpenAI in July.

Apple denied the allegations. It called the counterclaims "a transparent attempt to distract from the substance of Apple's lawsuit", according to reports, and denied using the employee to reach OpenAI's confidential information or trying to suppress competition. None of the claims on either side has been tested in court.

## What OpenAI alleges

OpenAI says an employee who left Apple, worked at OpenAI for about six months on its hardware effort and then returned to Apple had access to details of a new OpenAI device and its hardware roadmap. The filing says taking those documents "may have been his reason for joining OpenAI", according to reports. One report said the filing alleges the employee sent more than 100 confidential files to personal accounts before rejoining Apple. The filing does not name him.

OpenAI also accuses Apple of pressuring and threatening suppliers that make components for both companies, and says Apple's employment agreements are designed to "trap" staff and keep them from working on rival technology. It says Apple continues to access departing employees' personal devices and accounts after they leave, which it says lets Apple "monitor and ensnare" them. About 400 people have moved from Apple to OpenAI, the filing says. Reports describe the claims as including theft of trade secrets, interference with contracts and unfair competition; reports differ on how many counts are listed.

OpenAI says it is developing AI-powered personal devices that could "outcompete Apple on what Apple views as its own turf", according to reports.

## Apple's case

Apple sued OpenAI and two former Apple employees in July, alleging they misappropriated trade secrets to help OpenAI's consumer hardware project. OpenAI and the two former employees deny this and say Apple's case relied on unauthorised monitoring of one employee's personal messages, according to reports. In October, Apple dropped a request for an injunction after an agreement that OpenAI would not use any Apple confidential information, without any finding that anything had been taken, reports said.

## Why it matters

The dispute is part of a wider race to build devices designed around AI assistants rather than apps, which could challenge the smartphone's central place in people's lives. For India, where Apple now assembles a large share of its iPhones and where OpenAI has one of its biggest user bases, the outcome could shape which companies' devices and supply chains grow over the next few years.

## What happens next

Apple will have to respond to the counterclaims in court. No trial date has been reported.
